newsitem.title: UK: UK's Conservative Party ads win media coverage.
newsitem.headline: UK's Conservative Party ads win media coverage.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party has won more editorial coverage with its recent election advertising than any other advertiser, a report published on Thursday said.

London-based marketing consultancy Propeller said in a survey called "Ads that make the news" that British national newspapers ran 57 stories in the first quarter of 1997 about the Conservative's ad campaign, which was created by M&C Saatchi.
That compared with the opposition Labour Party's advertising campaign, which was written about on 24 occasions.
Britons have been bombarded by political advertising since Prime Minister John Major announced on March 17 that Britain's general election would take place on May 1.

"The Tories are gaining a great deal of (news) stories through high profile controversial ads. But not all publicity is good publicity -- many stories about the ads have criticised the Conservative's negative messages," said Propeller's managing director, Martin Loat.
On a related issue, Propeller said British newspapers were writing increasingly about the advertising industry.
National newspapers ran a total of 487 advertising news stories in the first quarter of 1997.

Of non-political advertisers, the telecoms giant, British Telecommunications Plc, received the most news coverage, followed closely by Pizza Hut and a recent ad campaign featuring Baywatch star, Pamela Anderson.
